JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be RC owner of the car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743 and injured filed application under Sec.166 of M.V.Act, claiming compensation/damages worth Rs.69,53,838/- from the respondents, owner, driver, insured and insurer of the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250, lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241, alleging that on 06.08.2020 at 7.40 p.m., on Yogeshwaranagar cross in front of Maruti Courier Company, on Hebbal ring road, when driving the car No.KA-03-MP-1743,
driver of a lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 negligently parked the same on the right lane of the road,
therefore, the car came in contact with the rear portion of the lorry, at that time driver of a car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 drove the same negligently dashed the same to the hind portion of the car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743, thereby caused accident, caused damage to the car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743 and caused injuries.
Shafakhat

2. In response to the notice, the respondents No.1, 2 and 5 appeared through their respective Advocates and on 07.09.2021 respondents No.1 & 2 and on 17.08.2023 respondent No.5 filed separate written statements denying the allegation regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.
3. Inspite of the service of notice, the respondents No.3 & 4/driver and owner of the lorry remained absent.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 24.09.2021 this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of SUV (Mahindra XUV) bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 and lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 by its drivers accident has occurred on 06.08.2020 to the petitioner who was riding a A Star (Maruthi-Suzuki) vehicle bearing No.KA-03-AP-1743 and he sustained injuries in the accident ?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the accident has occurred on account of negligent act of petitioner himself ?
3. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the accident has occurred on account of negligent act of lorry driver and petitioner ?

4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
5.
What order ?
5. On 9.11.2022, 21.01.2023, 27.02.2023, 30.03.2023, 27.06.203, 10.10.2023 and 10.1.2024 petitioner deposed as PW.1 and produced 31 documents at Exhibits P.1 to P.31.
On 25.07.2023 and 04.04.2024 respondent No.2/insurance company of the car produced evidence of the Officer as RW.1 and produced one document at Ex.R.1.

On 15.02.2024 and 14.04.2024 respondent No.5/insurer of the lorry produced evidence of an Officer as RW.2.
6.
On 24.06.2024, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner filed notes of argument along with two Judgments.
On 27.06.2024 learned advocate appearing for respondent No.2 filed notes of argument along with seven rulings.
7. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of the petitioner, respondent No.2 and 5 and perused the records.
8. In this case, respondent No.1 does not come forward to submit argument.

9. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:

Petitioner is entitled to receive Rs.1,59,000/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a.,as damages from the respondents.
Issue No.5 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue Nos.1 to 3 :- In the claim petition and evidence affidavit, PW.1/Petitioner stated that on 06.08.2020 at 7.40 p.m., when driving the car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743 on Hebbal ring road at Yogeshwarnagar cross, in front of Maruthi Courier Company, as driver of a lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 negligently parked same on the right lane of the road, his car came in contact with the hind part of the lorry, at the same time driver of the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the hind part of the car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to him and caused damage to car No.KA-03-MP-1743.
In the written statement, the respondent Nos. 1,2 and 5 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
In the written statement respondent No.1 asserted that due to the negligence of the petitioner, accident taken place.
In the written statement, respondent No.2/insurer of the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ- 0250 asserted that in view of the negligence of the petitioner and the driver of the lorry, accident taken place.
11. In the cross-examination PW.1 stated that on Hebbal ring road accident taken place, which is a busy road/area.
PW.1 admitted that a lorry was parked on the right lane of the road without taking precautions and explained that four boys are standing by providing signals.
PW.1 admitted that in the complaint noted that the lorry was parked without taking any precautions and placing hazardous lights.
PW.1 stated that police have filed chargesheet against the driver of the lorry alleging that lorry was parked without taking any precautionary measures.

In the cross-examination made on behalf of respondent No.5, PW.1 submitted that on the date of the accident, he was driving the car from Yeshwanthpura towards HBR layout and there was dense traffic in the evening hours.
PW.1 stated that from about more than 100 mtrs. distance, noticed the stationary lorry on the right side (on the) first lane.

PW.1 stated that there are four people standing near the stationary lorry,
among those four, two persons are behind the lorry and two persons are standing on the divider.
PW.1 admitted that if his car was not dashed by XUV car (KA-03-MZ-0250), he could not have dashed his car to the rear part of the stationary lorry.

12. In the evidence, RW.1/Office of respondent No.2/insurance company and in the evidence affidavit, RW.2-Officer of respondent No.5/insurer of the lorry submitted that they have not witnessed the accident.

13. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to Cr.No.85/2020 registered by Hebbal Traffic Police against driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 and car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 283 of IPC on the basis of the complaint dated 07.08.2020 presented by the petitioner.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the sketch which shows that on Hebbal ring road on the road leading towards Nagawara, collision taken place between car bearing Shafakhat.

4 No.KA-03-MP-1743, SUV car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 and lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the spot mahazar recorded on 07.08.2020.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of the statement of Sikandar Khan recorded on 07.08.2020.
Ex.P.5 is the statement of Sikandar Khan recorded on 11.08.2020.
Ex.P.10 is the copy of IMV report in which damage suffered by the lorry bearing No.KA-51-A- 9241, Car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743 and KA-03-MZ- 0250 in the accident are mentioned.

Ex.P.11 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Hebbal Traffic police against Naveen S/o Muddaveeranna-driver of the lorry for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279 and 283 of IPC and against Dinesh Kumar-driver of the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC.
In the chargesheet, name of the petitioner is mentioned as complainant and witness.
14. Exs.

P.12 to P.14 are the copy of the order sheet and accusation pertaining to CC No.3152/2020 on the file of MMTC-V, Bengaluru City, which shows that on the basis of the chargesheet, MMTC-V registered CC No.3152/2020 against Naveen and Dinesh Kumar/driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 and SUV car bearing No.KA-03- MZ-0250 for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279 and 283 of IPC, then on 02.11.2020, Naveen and Dinesh Kumar appeared before MMTC-V, Bengaluru, through their advocate, when MMTC-V readover and explained the accusation of the offense punishable under Sec.283, 279 of IPC to Naveen (driver of the lorry) and 279 of IPC to Dinesh Kumar (driver of the SUV)
, they pleaded guilty and suffered sentence of payment of fine worth of Rs.2,000/- and Rs.1,000/- respectively.
15. In this case, at this stage there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, it is clear that on 06.08.2020 at 7.40 p.m., when petitioner was driving a car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743 on Hebbal ring road near Yogeshwaranagar cross in front of Maruti Courier Company, driver of the lorry No.KA-51-A-9241 without taking precautionary measure parked the same on the right side lane, therefore car drove by the petitioner came in contact to the hind part of the lorry, at the same time Dinesh Kumar negligently drove the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250, dashed the same to the hind part of the car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743, thereby caused accident, caused damage to the car bearing No.KA-03-MP- 1743.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative, Issue No.2 in the negative and Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
16.Issue Nos.4 & 5 :

In the lengthy argument (notes of argument), learned advocate for the petitioner requested to estimate the compensation at Rs.69,53,838/- and a direction to the insurer of the offending vehicles (SUV and lorry) to deposit the same by relying on the following Judgments:
1.Civil Appeal No.8510/2022 DD-16.11.2022 (The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd., & Anr.)
2. MFA No.8051/2015(MV-DM) DD - 15.02.2024 (M/s ICON Petroleum Corpn.Ltd.
Vs. Shankar Murthy D & Anr.)
17.
In the notes of argument, learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 vehemently submitted that the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation amount, by relying on the Shafakhat.

sentences.text: In the light of the submission made on behalf of both the parties with reference to the Judgments/rulings cited above, I have appreciated the materials available in the file.

19. In the evidence affidavit and in claim petition, petitioner stated that in the accident suffered injuries to head, neck, abrasion, nervousness, mental shock, trauma, took treatment from Dr.
Vivekananda.M, Neuro Surgeon, by spending Rs.8,081/- and car suffered damage, M/s Pratham Motors Pvt.Ltd., estimated the cost of repair at Rs.2,59,909/- and charged Rs.5,900/- towards inspection and labour charges, spent Rs.3,700/- towards towing charges and the damaged car bearing No.KA-03-KP-1743 was replaced by a Wagon R worth of Rs.9,81,948/-.

20. In the written statement respondents No.1, 2 and 5 denied the allegation regarding nature of the injuries suffered and length of treatment taken by the petitioner and quantum of damages suffered by the petitioner.
21. In the cross-examination PW.1 stated that after accident, in view of the COVID-19 unable to visit the hospital, on next day went to Silver Line Diagnostics, HRBR layout.
PW.1 denied the suggestion about claiming of the damages from the insurer of his car bearing No.KA- 03-MP-1743.
PW.1 admitted receipt of the salary for the month of August, September and October,2020 and increase of his salary by year by year on the basis of performance.

PW.1 stated that finally on 09.02.2022 visited the hospital and as on 10.01.2024, earning Rs.65 Lakhs per annum.
22.
In the evidence affidavit, RW.1 stated that the respondent No.1 has not reported about the accident.
RW.1 stated in the cross-examination that as per IMV report, front part of the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 was damaged.

23. In the evidence affidavit, RW.2-Officer of the respondent No.5/insurance company asserted that the lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 was plied without permit, fitness certificate in contravention of the terms and conditions of the policy, therefore respondent No.5 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.4/insured of the lorry.
Shafakhat.

6 24.

In the cross-examination RW.2 admitted filing of the chargesheet by the police against the driver of the lorry which was registered as CC No.3152/2020.
25.

Medical bills shows that the petitioner has spent approximately Rs.25,858/- for treatment on 07.08.2020, 10.08.2020, 12.08.2021, 21.08.2021, 24.10.2021, 25.10.2021 and 09.02.2022.
26.

The bills produced at Sl.No.12 and 13 shows that the petitioner might have spent Rs.5,900/-
towards (car) body estimation charges, Rs.3,700/- towards towing charges on 12.08.2020 and 27.08.2020 respectively.
In the photos, damage suffered by car bearing No.KA-03-MP- 1743 and KA-03-MZ-0250 are visible.
27. Salary slip marked at Exs.P.12 and P.23 shows that during June 2020, July 2020, petitioner earned Rs.2,02,133/- per month as salary.
Salary slip marked at Ex.P.25 shows that during August 2020, September 2020 and October 2020, petitioner earned Rs.2,02,133/- p.m., as salary.
Ex . P.26
and P.27
are the copy of Income Tax return for the assessment year 2021-22 and challan.

In Ex.P.30, copy of the policy pertaining to car bearing No.KA- 03-MP-1743 for the period from 21.07.2020 to 20.07.2021 IDV is noted as Rs.1,59,000/-.
28.
In this case, medical/wound certificate about injuries might have suffered by the petitioner in the accident is not available.

29. As referred above, after investigation, police have filed chargesheet against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC,
driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.283 and 279 of IPC.
As referred above, the medical bills filed by the petitioner are not concerned to the injuries might have been suffered (by the petitioner) in the accident occurred on 06.08.2020.
Hence, it is clear that even though any injury suffered by the petitioner in the accident, he has neither suffered loss of salary nor decrease in the salary.
Hence, he is not entitled for any compensation (with respect to injuries alleged in the petition/evidence affidavit).
30. Copy of the RC marked at Ex.P.29 shows that during July 2011, car No.KA-03-MP-1743 has been manufactured.
The evidence on record shows that on 06.08.2020 car No.KA-03-MP-1743 met with an accident.

Considering the nature of the damage suffered by the car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743 noted in the IMV report and IDV noted in the Policy of the car marked at Ex.P.30, I have inferred that the petitioner is entitled for damages worth Rs.1,59,000/- from the respondents who are driver/owner/insured and insurer of the offending vehicles.

Hence, I answer Issue No.4 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of IMV Act is partly allowed in the following terms:
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,59,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Nine Thousand only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% per annum to the petitioner towards damages.
Shafakhat.

7

Respondents No.2 and 5 being the insurers of the SUV car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 and Lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 shall deposit compensation amount and interest at the ratio of 50 : 50 within two months from today.
After deposit of damages, the entire damages and interest shall be paid to the petitioner, by crediting the same to his bank account in accordance with law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 15 th day of July, 2024.)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.

2. In response to the notice, the respondents No.1, 2 and 5 appeared through their respective Advocates and on 07.09.2021 respondents No.1 & 2 and on 17.08.2023 respondent No.5 filed separate written statements denying the allegation regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.
3. Inspite of the service of notice, the respondents No.3 & 4/driver and owner of the lorry remained absent.
What order ?
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the pleadings on 24.09.2021 this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of SUV (Mahindra XUV) bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 and lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 by its drivers accident has occurred on 06.08.2020 to the petitioner who was riding a A Star (Maruthi-Suzuki) vehicle bearing No.KA-03-AP-1743 and he sustained injuries in the accident ?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the accident has occurred on account of negligent act of petitioner himself ?
3. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the accident has occurred on account of negligent act of lorry driver and petitioner ?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
5.
Hence, it is clear that on 06.08.2020 at 7.40 p.m., when petitioner was driving a car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743 on Hebbal ring road near Yogeshwaranagar cross in front of Maruti Courier Company, driver of the lorry No.KA-51-A-9241 without taking precautionary measure parked the same on the right side lane, therefore car drove by the petitioner came in contact to the hind part of the lorry, at the same time Dinesh Kumar negligently drove the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250, dashed the same to the hind part of the car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743, thereby caused accident, caused damage to the car bearing No.KA-03-MP- 1743.
opennyai_summary.facts:
In the written statement, respondent No.2/insurer of the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ- 0250 asserted that in view of the negligence of the petitioner and the driver of the lorry, accident taken place.
P.12 to P.14 are the copy of the order sheet and accusation pertaining to CC No.3152/2020 on the file of MMTC-V, Bengaluru City, which shows that on the basis of the chargesheet, MMTC-V registered CC No.3152/2020 against Naveen and Dinesh Kumar/driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 and SUV car bearing No.KA-03- MZ-0250 for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279 and 283 of IPC, then on 02.11.2020, Naveen and Dinesh Kumar appeared before MMTC-V, Bengaluru, through their advocate, when MMTC-V readover and explained the accusation of the offense punishable under Sec.283, 279 of IPC to Naveen (driver of the lorry) and 279 of IPC to Dinesh Kumar (driver of the SUV)
, they pleaded guilty and suffered sentence of payment of fine worth of Rs.2,000/- and Rs.1,000/- respectively.
20. In the written statement respondents No.1, 2 and 5 denied the allegation regarding nature of the injuries suffered and length of treatment taken by the petitioner and quantum of damages suffered by the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
15. In this case, at this stage there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.
29. As referred above, after investigation, police have filed chargesheet against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC,
driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.283 and 279 of IPC.
As referred above, the medical bills filed by the petitioner are not concerned to the injuries might have been suffered (by the petitioner) in the accident occurred on 06.08.2020.
Hence, it is clear that even though any injury suffered by the petitioner in the accident, he has neither suffered loss of salary nor decrease in the salary.
Hence, he is not entitled for any compensation (with respect to injuries alleged in the petition/evidence affidavit).
The evidence on record shows that on 06.08.2020 car No.KA-03-MP-1743 met with an accident.
Considering the nature of the damage suffered by the car bearing No.KA-03-MP-1743 noted in the IMV report and IDV noted in the Policy of the car marked at Ex.P.30, I have inferred that the petitioner is entitled for damages worth Rs.1,59,000/- from the respondents who are driver/owner/insured and insurer of the offending vehicles.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In the lengthy argument (notes of argument), learned advocate for the petitioner requested to estimate the compensation at Rs.69,53,838/- and a direction to the insurer of the offending vehicles (SUV and lorry) to deposit the same by relying on the following Judgments:
1.Civil Appeal No.8510/2022 DD-16.11.2022 (The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd., & Anr.)
2. MFA No.8051/2015(MV-DM) DD - 15.02.2024 (M/s ICON Petroleum Corpn.Ltd.
Vs. Shankar Murthy D & Anr.)
17.
In the notes of argument, learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 vehemently submitted that the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation amount, by relying on the Shafakhat.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, I answer Issue No.4 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of IMV Act is partly allowed in the following terms:
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,59,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Nine Thousand only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% per annum to the petitioner towards damages.
Shafakhat.
Respondents No.2 and 5 being the insurers of the SUV car bearing No.KA-03-MZ-0250 and Lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9241 shall deposit compensation amount and interest at the ratio of 50 : 50 within two months from today.
After deposit of damages, the entire damages and interest shall be paid to the petitioner, by crediting the same to his bank account in accordance with law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
